The Listening Room

drag the timeline · ← → step a day (shift = a week) · space = play · click a record on the monitor · F = fullscreen

Built from my YouTube Music and YouTube watch history, Aug 31, 2024 to Nov 5, 2026. The covers are YouTube thumbnails (album art for YouTube Music tracks), shrunk to 32 px and 24 colors; a few songs have none and show a plain tile. Moods, valence and energy are model estimates from title and artist, not measurements.

In the room: the lamp, rug, hoodie, neon sign, LED strip and record spines take the colors of the moods in the window. The window shows the hour played the most as Seattle would see it in that season: sunrise and sunset move from about 8:00 and 4:20 in winter to 5:10 and 9:10 in summer (a day-length formula, so approximate), with the Space Needle, evergreens, Rainier on clear days, cherry blossoms in spring, falling leaves in fall and string lights in winter. The desk changes too: cocoa, tulips, a fan, a pumpkin. The season comes from the middle of a 1-week or 1-month window and from the end of a 3-month or all-time window. Rain means the music sounds sadder than usual for a window of this length (summer swaps rain for marine-layer cloud, since Seattle summers are dry), sun means happier. The hi-fi follows the music: the pair of B&O Beovox CX100 speakers on stands breathes gently on the beat, the meters and spectrum rise with energy, the display scrolls the selected song, and the turntable spins its album. The head bobs with energy; the orange cat and the black cat share the rug, asleep when the window is calmer than the average and awake when it is not.
